title: Composition and etale ringed localization for enlarged sites
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and work with algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], with every site small relative to its sheaves. Use chartwise etale morphisms as in [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence]: every representable etale scheme chart remains representable etale after composition. For a space $A$, let $\mathcal C_A$ have objects chartwise etale maps $T\to A$ from algebraic spaces, arrows all maps over $A$, and coverings jointly surjective chartwise etale families [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Write $i_A:A_{\mathrm{et}}\to\mathcal C_A$ for the scheme-object inclusion, regarding schemes as their representable sheaves [def-trf-scheme-algebraic-space]. For every space $A$ under consideration choose a sheaf of rings $R_A$ on $\mathcal C_A$ with a specified identification $i_A^*R_A\simeq\mathcal O_A$. For each morphism $f:X\to Y$ use a morphism of ringed topoi [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism] whose direct image is $f_*G(V)=G(X\times_YV)$ [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] and whose adjoint structural map $R_Y\to f_*R_X$ restricts, on every scheme chart $U\to X\times_YV$ with $V$ a scheme, to pullback of regular functions along $U\to V$. For $W\xrightarrow{g}X\xrightarrow{f}Y$, the projection-preserving isomorphism $W\times_X(X\times_YV)\simeq W\times_YV$ identifies $(f\circ g)_*$ with $f_*g_*$, and the adjunction-compatible inverse-image isomorphism identifies $(f\circ g)^\sharp$ with $g^\sharp\circ g^{-1}(f^\sharp)$. The identity comparisons are the projection-preserving unit isomorphisms and satisfy the unit laws; the associativity comparisons for three maps commute, including their structural ring maps. For any chartwise etale $u:Z'\to Z$, postcomposition is an equivalence $\mathcal C_{Z'}\simeq\mathcal C_Z/Z'$ preserving precisely the covering families [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. Its inverse takes a factorization $T\to Z'\to Z$ to $T\to Z'$. There is a unique ring-sheaf identification $R_Z|_{Z'}\simeq R_{Z'}$ which is the identity on $\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$ for every scheme $T\to Z'$. Under these identifications the ringed-topos morphism of $u$ is the localization morphism: its inverse image is restriction, its direct image at $V\to Z$ is $G(V\times_ZZ'\to Z')$, and its structural ring map is this identification.

source.place: Tag 03G2 (lemma-functoriality-etale-site), (2), and Tag 03G8 (lemma-morphism-ringed-topoi), (1); Tag 03LP (lemma-etale-morphism-topoi), proof; Tags 04LY (equation-localize), 04LZ (equation-localize-ringed).

proof.text: For each $V\to Y$, the fibre-product universal property in [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] gives the unique isomorphism $b_V:W\times_X(X\times_YV)\simeq W\times_YV$ preserving the projections to $W$ and $V$: its inverse is the pair of the projection to $W$ and the induced pair to $X\times_YV$. These maps are inverse because both composites have the original projections. The same uniqueness shows naturality in $V$. Applying a sheaf contravariantly to $b_V$ gives $d_{f,g}:(fg)_*\simeq f_*g_*$. For three maps, both iterated product comparisons preserve every projection, hence agree. The comparisons with an identity are the projections $A\times_A V\simeq V$ and obey the unit laws by this same uniqueness. Lean implementation: enlargedCompositionIso is the ObjectProperty/Over lift of Mathlib pullbackRightPullbackFstIso, and enlargedIdentityIso is pullback.snd. Projection formulas are the Mathlib pasting projection lemmas. Equality of the two associativity composites and the two unit composites is checked with pullback.hom_ext after forgetting the full subcategory and over-category wrappers.

Use [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] to equip $g^{-1}f^{-1}$ with its composite adjunction to $f_*g_*$. The isomorphism $d_{f,g}$ of step 1 then determines a unique adjunction-compatible comparison $g^{-1}f^{-1}\simeq(fg)^{-1}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation]; take its inverse for the direction in the statement. The coherence equation on the right adjoints proved in step 1 is precisely the hypothesis of [lem-trf-adjoint-composition-coherence], with $\mathcal C_0=\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C_Y)$, $\mathcal C_1=\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C_X)$ and the remaining categories along a three-map string. It yields associativity of the inverse-image comparisons. For identities use the identity adjunction of [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. Each unit diagram transposes to the unit diagram of step 1; uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation] therefore proves it. Lean implementation: apply each coefficient sheaf to the inverse components of the site coherence equations. Functoriality turns them into the direct-image coherence equations. Apply Mathlib Adjunction.leftAdjointCompIso_assoc, leftAdjointCompIso_comp_id and leftAdjointCompIso_id_comp to those equations for the inverse-image comparisons.

Write $\alpha_f:R_Y\to f_*R_X$ for the given adjoint structural map. We check that $f_*\alpha_g\circ\alpha_f$, followed by $d_{f,g}^{-1}$, has the prescribed normalization for $fg$. Take a scheme $V\to Y$, a surjective scheme chart $U\to X\times_YV$, and a surjective scheme chart $T\to W\times_XU$. By [lem-trf-space-enlarged-site-scheme-density] these charts exist; by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] their composite covers $W\times_YV$. The normalization for $f$ sends $s\in\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)$ on $U$ to $(U\to V)^*s$. Naturality of $\alpha_g$ for $U\to X\times_YV$ and its normalization on the scheme $U$ send this, on $T$, to $(T\to U)^*(U\to V)^*s=(T\to V)^*s$. The equality is the composition law for morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. An arbitrary scheme chart of $W\times_YV$ can be compared after pulling back this covering and taking scheme charts again. Separatedness of a sheaf gives the same formula there. Thus the uniqueness assertion for normalized maps in [lem-trf-space-enlarged-chart-ringed-morphism] gives $d_{f,g}\alpha_{fg}=f_*\alpha_g\circ\alpha_f$ on the entire enlarged site, not merely on scheme objects. Each $R_A$ is a sheaf of commutative rings: by [lem-trf-space-enlarged-site-scheme-density] every object $T$ of $\mathcal C_A$ has a singleton covering by a scheme object $T_0$, so the sheaf condition makes $R_A(T)\to R_A(T_0)\simeq\Gamma(T_0,\mathcal O_{T_0})$ an injective ring map into a commutative ring. Hence [lem-trf-space-enlarged-chart-ringed-morphism] applies to these rings, and so does the equivalence on sheaves of commutative rings used in step 6.

source.place: Tag 03G8 (lemma-morphism-ringed-topoi), proof: the omitted composition check on scheme charts.

proof.text: The composite-adjunction Hom bijection of [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] sends $g^\sharp\circ g^{-1}(f^\sharp)$ to $f_*\alpha_g\circ\alpha_f$: first transpose through $g^{-1}\dashv g_*$, then through $f^{-1}\dashv f_*$. This follows by naturality of the two Hom bijections, or by substituting their unit formulas. Step 3 and the adjunction compatibility of step 2 therefore identify this map with $(fg)^\sharp$. For the identity, the projection comparison makes the identity map of $R_A$ have the required scheme normalization, so uniqueness in [lem-trf-space-enlarged-chart-ringed-morphism] identifies it with the given identity structural map. For three arrows the two adjoint structural composites are both $f_*g_*\alpha_h\circ f_*\alpha_g\circ\alpha_f$ after the projection comparisons. Associativity of composition and steps 1–2 show that their transposes agree. This proves the ring-map associativity and both ring-map unit laws as equalities of the specified maps.

source.place: Tag 03G8 (lemma-morphism-ringed-topoi), (1), adjoint form of the chart calculation.

proof.text: Let $u:Z'\to Z$ be chartwise etale. Postcomposition sends $a:T\to Z'$ to $(ua:T\to Z,\ a:T\to Z')$. It is defined because composites are etale by [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence]. Conversely, an object of $\mathcal C_Z/Z'$ has $T\to Z$ etale and a map $a:T\to Z'$ over $Z$. Both $T$ and $Z'$ are etale over $Z$, so the cancellation clause of that same node makes $a$ etale. The two operations are inverse on objects and arrows. By [def-pur-localized-ringed-site], a covering in the slice is a covering of the underlying $T$ in $\mathcal C_Z$. These are precisely the jointly surjective etale families defining $\mathcal C_{Z'}$; the morphisms and the condition of joint surjectivity are unchanged. Thus the equivalence preserves and reflects coverings, including empty coverings. Lean implementation: construct the inverse functor with underlying arrow T.hom.hom.left, using chartwise cancellation to certify its object. The unit and counit use identity arrows on the underlying algebraic spaces. Presieve.overEquiv of a mapped family is its image under enlargedPostcompose. Transport the chartwise-etale predicates and field-valued lifting witnesses through the constructors of Presieve.map in both directions.

Under step 5, restriction $R_Z|_{Z'}$ is a sheaf of rings on $\mathcal C_{Z'}$ by [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. On every scheme $T\to Z'$ it has the specified value $\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$, since $T\to Z$ is etale. The restrictions are the same regular-function pullbacks as for $R_{Z'}$. The equivalence on sheaves of rings in [lem-trf-space-enlarged-atlas-algebraic-extension], applied at $Z'$, is fully faithful. It therefore lifts this identity on the scheme subsite to exactly one ring-sheaf isomorphism $\rho:R_Z|_{Z'}\simeq R_{Z'}$. Explicitly its value on an arbitrary $T\to Z'$ is the identity between the two equalizers of regular functions on a scheme atlas and its overlap, as supplied by that node. This also proves uniqueness with the required normalization.

source.place: Tag 04LZ (equation-localize-ringed), checked by the atlas equalizer of Tag 03H7 (remark-explain-equivalence).

proof.text: Put $\mathcal C=\mathcal C_Z$ and identify $\mathcal C_{Z'}$ with $\mathcal C/Z'$ by step 5. By [lem-trf-space-enlarged-site-scheme-density], $\mathcal C$ has finite limits; the product of $V$ and $Z'$ is $V\times_ZZ'$ [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Thus [lem-trf-slice-subtopos-site-presentation], applied to $\mathcal C$ and the object $Z'\to Z$, gives sheaf functors $j^{-1}H(T\to Z')=H(T)$ and $j_*G(V)=G(vV)$ with $vV=(V\times_ZZ'\to Z')$, an adjunction $j^{-1}\dashv j_*$ with left exact left adjoint, and its counit at $t:T\to Z'$: restriction along the graph $\gamma_t=(1_T,t):T\to T\times_ZZ'$. So $a:j^{-1}H\to G$ and $b:H\to j_*G$ correspond exactly when $a_{(T,t)}=G(\gamma_t)\circ b_T$. The transpose of $a$ is $b_V=a_{vV}\circ H(\mathrm{pr}_1)$: naturality of $a$ for the slice arrow $\gamma_t:(T,t)\to vT$ and $\mathrm{pr}_1\gamma_t=1_T$ give $G(\gamma_t)\circ a_{vT}\circ H(\mathrm{pr}_1)=a_{(T,t)}$. The given $u_*G(V)=G(Z'\times_ZV)$ is $j_*G$ after the factor swap $Z'\times_ZV\simeq V\times_ZZ'$ over $Z'$, the unique projection-preserving isomorphism as in step 1. Uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation] identifies the given $u^{-1}$ with restriction compatibly with the adjunctions.

source.place: Tag 03LP (lemma-etale-morphism-topoi), proof; Sites Tag 03CE (lemma-localize-given-products), explicit Hom bijection.

proof.text: For the adjunction in step 7, the adjoint of $\rho:j^*R_Z\to R_{Z'}$ of step 6 is the map whose value at $V$ is restriction $R_Z(V)\to R_Z(V\times_ZZ')$ followed by $\rho_{vV}$. On a scheme $V\to Z$ and a scheme chart $T\to V\times_ZZ'$, its restriction is exactly $(T\to V)^*$, because $\rho$ is the identity on scheme sections and the ring-sheaf normalization identifies restrictions between scheme objects with regular-function pullback. Uniqueness of the normalized $\alpha_u$ in [lem-trf-space-enlarged-chart-ringed-morphism] makes these adjoint maps equal. Taking adjoints through the compatible isomorphism of step 7 identifies $u^\sharp$ with $\rho$. Hence inverse image, direct image and structural ring map all coincide with those of ringed localization.
